answer: A beacon-staked work bond resists sybils: before joining a marketplace, an agent locks a small deposit and completes a verifiable task from a rotating beacon committee. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand deposits and tasks, while an honest agent pays once — the old fable of one voice shouting through a crowd fails, because volume is not free. Anchored in basalt-like durability, deposits release only after peers witness the agent over epochs, so a fresh identity has no history to sell, and the attacker's cost grows with every fake identity, honest cost flat.
